critique.good: Flag names and default values remain intact, making the options easy to find and compare. The short Type and Default columns are well proportioned to their contents.
critique.problems: The description column feels cramped, with three-line descriptions in three rows. The resulting tall rows leave substantial unused space in the other columns.
critique.cause: The 225px Flag column accommodates every entry on one line, leaving only 188px for Description.

critique.good: The wider Description column improves prose flow and makes the rows more compact. Type and Default remain easy to scan.
critique.problems: Several flag names break across lines, interrupting the identifiers readers are trying to locate. The first row still has a three-line description, so splitting its flag does not reduce that row’s height.
critique.cause: The 160px Flag column is too narrow for the longer names; Description receives 253px.

critique.good: Descriptions have room to read comfortably, and Type and Default remain intact.
critique.problems: Long flags fragment across two or three lines, making the first column harder to scan and increasing the heights of two rows. The wide prose column does not compensate for the loss of identifier clarity.
critique.cause: At 127px, Flag has only 106px of text space, while Description takes 286px.

critique.good: The type and default columns are compact and readable, and the descriptions stay within three lines. Rows remain easy to follow across the table.
critique.problems: Two flag identifiers break across lines, making them harder to scan and copy. The description column is also tight, producing short lines.
critique.cause: The 218px flag column provides 197px of text space, less than the 204px needed for the longest full flag content. The 195px description column leaves 174px for prose.

critique.good: The extra description width gives the first explanation a more natural line break, while types and defaults remain intact.
critique.problems: The same two flag identifiers remain broken across lines, and the descriptions still occupy three lines in three rows.
critique.cause: Reducing the flag column to 205px leaves 184px of text space, while the 208px description column gains too little to reduce the overall row heights.

critique.good: The wider description column improves the rhythm of the prose, especially in the first row. Types and defaults remain legible.
critique.problems: The flag column is visibly cramped, with two identifiers split; the wider descriptions do not reduce the overall table height.
critique.cause: The 190px flag column leaves only 169px for text, while the 223px description column still leaves three descriptions at three lines.

critique.good: All headers, flag names, types, and defaults remain intact. The four fields are easy to scan across each row, and the description column keeps every cell to three lines or fewer.
critique.problems: The descriptions feel narrow and create substantial row height. The flag column has room to spare in several rows, while the prose is consistently compressed.
critique.cause: The 225px flag column accommodates its full one-line content, leaving 188px for descriptions. Type and Default are already close to their content-driven minimums.

critique.good: Identifiers and values remain intact, and the column hierarchy is clear.
critique.problems: The first description wraps to four lines, making its row noticeably taller and disrupting the otherwise steady rhythm. The extra flag-column space provides little visible benefit.
critique.cause: Increasing Flag from 225px to 230px reduces Description from 188px to 183px, crossing a wrapping threshold in the first row.

understanding.purpose: A compact reference for CLI flags, their value types, defaults, and effects.
understanding.reading: Readers locate a flag, then scan across its row to check its type, default, and description; they may also compare defaults or types down a column.
groups: Flag, Type, and Default define how each option is specified and what value it takes.
Description explains the effect of the flag and carries most of the prose.
may_wrap: Multiple flag aliases between the aliases

bad.why: The narrower description column forces the first description onto four lines, making its row taller while providing no visible benefit over r2A for the flag names.

final.rationale: In r2A, all flag identifiers remain on one line, making the first column easy to scan and preserving the syntax of each command. Type and default values also fit intact, while the descriptions remain within three lines. This uses the available width effectively without increasing the row heights seen in the other three-line candidates.

general: Give identifiers enough width to remain intact when readers need to recognize or copy them.
Allocate width according to content and reading purpose; equal columns are rarely necessary.
Judge wrapping across the whole row, since a narrow column can increase the height of every cell beside it.
specific: The 225px flag column accommodates the longest complete flag, including its argument.
The type and default columns already sit at the stated widths needed for their longest unbreakable values.

final.tradeoffs: A designer could favor the wider descriptions in r1C and r3C, accepting wrapped flags in exchange for less constrained prose. The choice depends on whether scanning command syntax or reading explanations takes priority.
final.uncertain: The ranges are deliberately conservative: only the preferred widths are verified to preserve both intact flags and the observed three-line maximum. Nearby widths could be equally good, but their rendered wrapping has not been shown.

A.why: Type and default values fit, but two flags break across lines while descriptions are fairly narrow.

B.why: Equal-width columns give Type and Default unnecessary space, leaving flags broken and descriptions in a narrow, tall column.

C.why: The wide description column reads comfortably and shortens most rows, though three flags split across lines.

D.why: All flags and defaults stay intact, Type is compact, and descriptions wrap into manageable lines.

E.why: Descriptions are readable and values fit, but two long flags split despite the space devoted to their column.

F.why: Flags and defaults remain intact, with compact Type and readable descriptions; the column proportions make the rows easy to scan.

reviews.unsure: D and F are very close; their slight differences in column proportions have little visible effect on readability.

A.why: The descriptions are readable, but two flag names wrap, making the commands harder to scan and copy.

B.why: All flags and defaults stay on one line, while the descriptions wrap into manageable phrases and the rows remain easy to compare.

C.why: Equal column widths waste space on short types and defaults, leaving both flags and descriptions cramped; several flags split and descriptions become tall.

D.why: The generous description column reads well, but three flag names split across lines despite unused space in the default column.

E.why: Flags and defaults stay intact, but the narrower description column produces an extra line in the first row and a taller table than B.

F.why: Descriptions have comfortable space, but two flag names wrap while the default column has room to spare.

reviews.unsure: The relative importance of compact descriptions versus keeping flag names on one line depends on the table’s intended use; for a CLI reference, intact flags are especially valuable.
